verdict.rationale: Whether source code is available under an open license is a fair question for any software product, including a meeting-notes app, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence shows Granola publishing its source or using an open license; the docs cover only a hosted API, an MCP server and an OpenAPI spec, which are integration surfaces, not source access. Community comments mention seeking open-source alternatives but do not document a Granola license.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license
